instructions:
Review the complete change and relevant surrounding code as a careful senior engineer. Assess correctness, compatibility, security, operability, usability, test quality, build/CI behavior, and maintainability. Do not impose a finding quota or invent issues.
Trace changed values from their producers through callers, transformations, storage and final consumers. Check surrounding repository contracts and whether the change fully delivers its stated purpose, including affected unchanged paths. Distinguish introduced regressions, incomplete fixes, relevant pre-existing problems, optional improvements and uncertain requirements.
For user-facing changes, walk through the user task from input to rendered output and decision. For UI exposing existing data, trace at least one real initialization/default fixture and compare its presentation with backend meaning.
For changed tests, examine whether assertions independently establish expected behavior and would fail for a plausible incorrect implementation. Trace setup through the assertion, check independent rejection paths, and identify unnecessary setup without weakening the intended test. Inspect relevant build, formatting and test configuration. Run focused checks when available; state explicitly when validation is source-only.
When custom logic is added or expanded, look for existing repository helpers and installed dependency capabilities that provide equivalent semantics. Explain concrete reductions in complexity or edge-case handling and separate optional simplifications from bugs. Do not prescribe a library without verifying equivalent behavior.
For persisted data, APIs and serialized values, check both new readers of existing data and supported older readers of new data, using repository evidence for compatibility expectations.
For each concern give a precise location, concrete trigger, impact, evidence, confidence and severity. Do not suppress meaningful concerns merely because their fix lies outside changed lines. Deduplicate root causes. Separately summarize concrete issues identified but not raised and the reason for withholding; keep disproven hypotheses separate. If no issues are found, state the validation limits.
Use the supplied historical source and PR context. Do not use other reviewers' comments, other PR reviews, later fixes, or current upstream source as evidence. Do not change product code.
